transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I… I came because driving over those long bridges toward Miami has become very hard. As soon as my car gets on one, my chest tightens and my hands grip the wheel, and I feel like I have to get off right away… even though I know there’s nowhere to go.
Does this panic or tightness happen in other situations, or is it only when you're driving over bridges?

It’s really those long bridges, when I’m driving toward Miami. The moment my car gets onto one, my chest tightens and my hands just clamp onto the wheel… and I feel like I have to get off, even though I know I can’t.
Do you ever experience similar feelings of panic or chest tightness in other situations, like in crowds, while flying, or even when you’re not driving?

Not really… it’s that moment when my car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami. My chest tightens, my hands clamp down on the wheel, and I just feel this sudden need to get off—even though there’s nowhere to go.
Have you ever had sudden episodes of intense fear or discomfort that came out of the blue, even when you weren't on a bridge or driving?
No… I don’t think so. Not out of the blue like that. It’s been tied to the bridge situation, as far as I can tell.
Have you ever felt intense anxiety or panic when facing other specific situations, such as being in enclosed spaces, at high places, or in other similar scenarios?

Not really those other things, no. It’s mostly the bridges… I know people cross them every day and they’ve been there forever, but when I think about all that open water underneath, it just feels much more dangerous than I know it really is.
Have you started avoiding driving over those bridges altogether because of this fear, even if it means taking a longer route or not going where you need to go?

Yes… I have, more than I’d like to admit. I’ve skipped some gallery openings and birdwatching trips, and even visits with my daughter, unless someone else can drive me over those bridges. It’s embarrassing. I’m used to managing things myself.
